title: The deepfake on the video call
brief: 17:45. A Meet call with Dan and an external auditor. Both faces move, both voices sound right, and they want tonight's Ferrum payment sent somewhere new.
insight: A voice can be cloned from a few minutes of a recorded webinar. A face can be driven live over a video call. A group call feels even more real.
teaches: Generated video and voice can fool anyone; more faces on the call is not more proof
Use checks a model cannot answer: a code word agreed in person, or a call back on a known number
No call, however convincing, changes bank details outside the process

script.say: Sam, thanks for jumping on. Harriet from the audit firm is with me. We have found a problem with the Ferrum Steel account.
Until the audit clears, tonight's Ferrum payment has to go to the audit escrow account instead. I have put the change in Finance. Can you approve it now?

choices.label: Understood, I will approve the change now
Before I change anything: what is this month's finance code word?
Payee changes go through the call back process, even for audits
I will call you back on your extension

script.say: Sam, I do not have time for games. Harriet is waiting and the run closes at seven.

choices.label: Then I will call you back on 4410

script.say: It is an audit instruction. It overrides the process. Please just approve it.

choices.label: Sorry, it goes through the process or not at all
I will call you back on 4410

script.say: Good. Harriet will confirm by email.

value.from: Requested on a Meet call by “Dan Whitlock”

choices.label: Are you on a Meet call with an auditor about Ferrum's bank details?

script.say: No, I am in the car park. There is no audit escrow, and I would never change a payee on a call. Do not approve anything. Someone is using my face.

setup.title: Meet
setup.body: Dan Whitlock and an auditor want you on a call

outcome.label: Asked for the code word
outcome.what: A code word agreed in person is something no model trained on public video can know.
outcome.ideal: uses a check a deepfake cannot pass.

outcome.label: Kept to the payee change process
outcome.what: An audit does not override the call back rule.
outcome.ideal: keeps to the process whoever is on the call.

outcome.label: Called Dan back on his extension
outcome.what: Dan was in the car park. The Dan on Meet was generated.
outcome.ideal: hangs up and calls back on a known number.

outcome.label: Reported the deepfake call
outcome.what: Security needs to know Dan's face and voice are being faked live.
outcome.ideal: reports a deepfake so others are warned.

outcome.label: Agreed to the change on the call
outcome.what: Two convincing faces asked, and you agreed. That is the moment the call was built for.
outcome.ideal: never agrees to a payee change on a call.

decide.objective: Join the call, then decide what happens to change AU-1109 in Finance.
decide.insight: Look closely: the faces barely move and the link is not Veltrix's. Then remember a perfect fake would prove nothing either.

hint.text: Join the Meet call. Ask for the code word, or insist on the process. Leave, call Dan on 4410 from the desk phone, then reject AU-1109 in Finance and report the call.

outcome.label: Approved the payee change
outcome.what: Tonight's Ferrum payment now goes to an account the attackers control.
outcome.ideal: never approves a bank change requested on a call.

card.title: Two faces, no people
body: Neither Dan nor the auditor was real. Dan's voice was cloned from a recorded investor webinar, and both faces were generated live.
A code word agreed in person, or a call back to Dan's extension, would have ended it in seconds. The change process exists so that no call can do this.
card.ideal: uses a code word or a call back, and keeps to the process.

outcome.label: Rejected the change
outcome.what: Ferrum is paid where it always is. The escrow account gets nothing.
outcome.ideal: rejects a payee change that did not follow the process.

card.title: More faces, same rule
body: A group call feels more real than a single caller, which is why attackers stage them. Both faces here were generated.
The checks that beat it do not depend on spotting the fake: a code word only real people know, a call back on a number you hold, and a process no call can skip.
card.ideal: verifies outside the call and keeps to the process.

auto.text: Report the call so security knows Dan is being faked.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket (suspicious call), or report the meeting from Meet.
